Implement Correlation rules logsource conditions

Rather than return false for all Correlation rules, change the behavior
of the log source condition pipeline to check each of the rules
referenced in the Correlation rule and test their logsources. The
logsource must fully match one or more of those rules in order to return
true.

This implementation operates recursively, checking rules that are nested
within correlated Correlation rules.

subject: Implemented a better date conversion for 'date:' and 'modified:' fields.
message:
Implemented a better date conversion for 'date:' and 'modified:' fields.

This PR fixes the following bad dates that were accepted previously:
  *  date: 01-01-24 was accepted as 0001-01-24
  *  date: 24-01-24 was accepted as 0024-01-24

These will result in an error now.

Recently in 300d61e08624a0eb154343a878ff2d87d8436934 the US-style dates
were eliminated. Unfortunately, these are still very much used.
I propose we continue supporting such dates, but we only accept unambiguous forms.

Therefore, this commit implements and tests the dates of the following formats:
   * XXXX-XX-XX   -- fully corresponds to yaml date format
   * XXXX/XX/XX, XXXX/XX/X, XXXX/X/XX, XXXX/X/X -- legacy, often occurs in (old) US-based sigmas

subject: Initial design for fieldref wildcard support
message:
Initial design for fieldref wildcard support

Field references can currently only specify a full match on two fields,
but for backends that support it, we have found that in practice being
able to partially match one field against another is important. This
commit introduces the ability for a field reference to have a leading
or trailing wildcard and updates the contains, startswith, and endswith
modifiers to allow the rule to set them.

subject: fix: use stable cache key independent of URL in mitre_attack and mitre_d3fend
message:
fix: use stable cache key independent of URL in mitre_attack and mitre_d3fend

Previously the cache key included the URL (e.g. "mitre_attack_data_./enterprise-attack.json"),
so data pre-populated via `update-cache --url mitre_attack:./file.json` was stored under a
URL-specific key. When `sigma check` ran in a fresh process with no custom URL set, it looked
for "mitre_attack_data_default" - a different key - got a cache miss, and attempted a network
download, breaking offline/restricted-network usage.

Fix: use a stable key ("mitre_attack_data" / "mitre_d3fend_data") so any pre-populated cache
entry is found regardless of the source URL. set_url() already calls clear_cache() to force
re-download when the source changes, so correctness is maintained.

subject: fix: don't disable to_plain() conversion for pure field name mappings
message:
fix: don't disable to_plain() conversion for pure field name mappings

When FieldMappingTransformationBase performs a 1:1 field rename (e.g.,
User → UserName), only the field name attribute changes — the values
list is not replaced. The parent DetectionItemTransformation.apply_detection()
was unconditionally calling disable_conversion_to_plain() on any
returned SigmaDetectionItem, preventing SigmaRule.to_dict() from
working even when the original_value is still valid.

Fix: Override apply_detection() in FieldMappingTransformationBase to
compare the identity of detection_item.value before and after the
transformation. Only call disable_conversion_to_plain() when a new
value list was assigned (i.e., values actually changed — as happens
with keyword-to-field mappings that add wildcards, or field-reference
mappings). A pure field rename keeps the same list object, so
original_value remains valid and to_plain() correctly serializes the
current state with the renamed field.

Fixes: SigmaRule.to_dict() raises SigmaError after field_name_mapping

subject: Bound external source response sizes
message:
Bound external source response sizes

Add size caps so a hostile or oversized external source cannot exhaust
memory: HTTPPlaceholderTransformation streams the response and aborts
once max_body_size bytes have been read, and CommandPlaceholderTransformation
rejects stdout larger than max_stdout. Both default to 10 MiB and are
configurable per source. Note: the command path still buffers stdout in
memory before the check (subprocess.run); a true streaming cap there is
left as follow-up.

subject: Make CSV column-index mode consistent about header rows
message:
Make CSV column-index mode consistent about header rows

Column-name CSV parsing used csv.DictReader, which consumes the header
row, while column-index parsing used csv.reader, which did not, so the
header cell leaked through as a value. Add a csv_has_header flag
(default True): index mode now skips the header to match name mode, and
name mode raises a clear error when csv_has_header is False since a
column name cannot be resolved without a header.

subject: Reject non-scalar jq results for placeholder replacement
message:
Reject non-scalar jq results for placeholder replacement

A placeholder replacement becomes an individual field match value, so a
jq_expression that returns an array or object is a user error: str() of
a container previously leaked a Python repr (e.g. "['a', 'b']") into the
rule as a single match value. Reject dict/list results with a clear error
pointing at scalar projection (e.g. '.items[]' instead of '.items');
scalars are unchanged.

subject: Validate external source format at construction time
message:
Validate external source format at construction time

The data format was only checked lazily inside _parse_data, so a typo in
`format` surfaced at rule-apply time instead of when the transformation
was built. Validate it in ExternalSourceBaseTransformation.__post_init__
(against plaintext/csv/json/yaml) and have the subclasses chain through
super().__post_init__() so the check runs for all of them.

subject: Narrow HTTP fetch error handling to requests.RequestException
message:
Narrow HTTP fetch error handling to requests.RequestException

The HTTP fetch caught bare Exception, masking unexpected non-network
errors as "failed to fetch" and requiring a guard to avoid swallowing the
max_body_size SigmaValueError. Catch only requests.RequestException so
connection, timeout and HTTP-status failures are wrapped while the size
cap error and genuine bugs propagate unchanged.
